audit.whatIsWrong: Content-layer prose (early/mid/late/whys/spikes/wants) misgenders Janna with she/her throughout.
audit.why: The project's authoritative gender list (champ-data/champ-gender.js / the audit brief's roster) does not include janna among the female champions in this lane's slice, so the pronoun convention here defaults to he/him. The full layer already avoids gendered pronouns for Janna (correct), but champ-data/content/sup/rell.js uses she/her consistently, which is the misgendering pattern called out by the defect catalogue.
audit.corrected: Swap she/her/hers to he/him/his throughout early, mid, late, all 7 whys, all 4 spikes[].text, and the wants.you/wants.foe bullets that reference her.

audit.why: Janna is a pure disengage/peel enchanter; Rell is a hard-engage tank with no way to force a fight through Zephyr slow, Howling Gale knockup, and Monsoon. Content already frames this correctly as Tricky/7-10.

content.spikes already tracks the real power-spike pattern: level 2 disengage denies the W all-in, level 6 Monsoon hard-counters Magnet Storm, and the matchup only opens up when her R/Q are baited out.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[N].side in the full layer is the unaudited placeholder "Skill" on all 7 rows, while content win[] and the packet levelChart both independently agree Janna wins every stage (packet: 49.21% win rate for Rell = Janna favored, no defect flagged, chart ["Janna"]x7 matches win[]).
audit.why: Since win[] already reads Janna for all 7 rows and no contradiction exists between the packet and the content layer, only phases[].side needs to be synced to stop the two layers from showing different winners for the same row.
audit.corrected: Set phases[0..6].side to "Janna"; no win[] edit needed since it already reads Janna.

edits.before: Janna is the disengage answer to your hard engage, so the level 1-2 phase favors her — the instant you W-slam in, her Q knockup and Zephyr slow peel you right back off her ADC. Don't waste your engage into a full-health Janna with cooldowns up; poke and freeze instead. Ward for the jungler because a coordinated gank is how you actually get a kill through her peel.
edits.after: Janna is the disengage answer to your hard engage, so the level 1-2 phase favors his — the instant you W-slam in, his Q knockup and Zephyr slow peel you right back off his ADC. Don't waste your engage into a full-health Janna with cooldowns up; poke and freeze instead. Ward for the jungler because a coordinated gank is how you actually get a kill through his peel.

edits.before: From 3-6 she keeps shielding and slowing every trade you try to force. Your dismount burst is real, but her shields and Zephyr blunt it and reposition you off target. Treat your W stun as a pick tool on an isolated target, and set up with your jungler rather than swinging lane trades she always wins on disengage.
edits.after: From 3-6 he keeps shielding and slowing every trade you try to force. Your dismount burst is real, but his shields and Zephyr blunt it and reposition you off target. Treat your W stun as a pick tool on an isolated target, and set up with your jungler rather than swinging lane trades he always wins on disengage.

edits.before: On items the stat check is yours but the fight script is hers: Monsoon undoes your Magnet Storm engage and her shields keep her carry topped. Bait her R with a feint, then commit for real. Look to catch her ADC in the side lanes where no tornado or monsoon is up to bail them out.

edits.before: You get W (Ferromancy: Crash Down) at 2 and want to slam-engage, but Janna's Q (Howling Gale) and W (Zephyr) exist to punish exactly that — her monkey's-paw disengage means every all-in you start she can peel back. Only commit if her Q is on cooldown, and expect her to slow you with W the moment you dismount-stun her ADC.
